prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 topological insulators, and its first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged from round 1: a single-part prize for B013 to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. After the full exchange I rest it on the scientific closure and not on the support count, which the chair rightly says is partly an effect of members reading each other's openings. Kane and Mele showed that spin-orbit coupling plus time-reversal symmetry gives a Z2 classification with protected helical edge states. Molenkamp's group then measured the predicted edge conductance in HgTe wells, with the quantised value, the gate-voltage dependence and the length and width dependence that exclude trivial explanations. A sharp quantitative prediction was tested in a device built to realise it, and the result has been reproduced by transport and spectroscopy in several material families for roughly eighteen years. Maturity is therefore not in doubt. On the chair's question about 2016: that prize rewarded topological phase transitions and Hall-type phases of model and thin-film systems, whereas this one rewards symmetry-protected band topology, in which a time-reversal-invariant insulator in a real material with strong spin-orbit coupling carries protected boundary states. I can state that in one sentence, and I would accept it as sufficient. I would keep the citation tied to the quantum spin Hall state and its first observation, as Pearce suggests, so that it does not claim more for the three named people than they did.
statement.case_against: The allocation remains a judgment and not a clean ranking. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe realisation that told Molenkamp where to look, and Zhang's death removes one possible laureate. Hasan's ARPES work on 3D topological insulators is an original and decisive experiment that a 2D-based trio leaves out, so the committee must be open that any trio excludes someone with a serious claim. Danielsson's wording, ending on topological insulators as a new class of matter, would reach into the 3D branch and so claim more than the three names support. A second topology prize after 2016 also needs the plain statement of difference above, and device applications are still scarce, although the statutes reward the discovery and not the application.

responses.point: Eriksson has withdrawn his opening swap of Mele for Hasan and says he can accept the Kane, Mele and Molenkamp trio provided the citation is clear about what the experiment shows.
responses.response: I am glad we now agree on the names. I accept your condition on the citation: it should say that Molenkamp's group observed the edge-channel conduction in HgTe wells, and it should not say that the experiment proved spin-polarised transport in every detail, because the nonlocal interpretations were debated. I also agree with your underlying concern. Hasan's 3D work is what made topological insulators a materials field, and I would not want the final record to imply otherwise. I would rather the committee note that clearly in its discussion than give Hasan a seat taken from Mele, since Mele co-authored both Z2 papers. If you or others later find a configuration with a defensible 3D part, that would be a separate recognition and should not be built into this prize.

responses.point: Kroll is the sole supporter of B006 for Katori and Ye, with two clean names and 10^-18 comparisons between laboratories, and he names B013 as his first alternative. He also pressed me on the overlap of circuit QED (B009) with the 2025 prize and on Girvin's absence from the credit.
responses.response: I take the B009 point and now agree. Girvin co-authored the 2004 proposal, and a second superconducting-circuit prize one year after 2025 would need an explanation I cannot give you honestly, so B009 should not be in my preferred configuration. Given that and my conflict, I have also replaced it in my alternatives with B006. On substance, I find the lattice clock comparisons persuasive, and this is the strongest reproducibility case of any candidate on the list, since independent strontium and ytterbium clocks agree at the 10^-18 level. I still rank B013 first because the discovery of a new regime of physics seems to me more in keeping with the statutes than an instrument refinement, and because of the frequency-comb context of 2005. I would ask you the specific question of what, in your view, is physically new in the lattice clock beyond the earlier trapped-ion clocks. If the answer is the magic-wavelength condition together with many-atom statistics, I think the citation could be worded around that and I would then be comfortable with B006 as an alternative.

responses.point: Lindroth prefers B002 for Bloch, Greiner and Zoller, treats it as a discovery about emergent many-body matter, and she argues that 2016 lowers the novelty of a second topological prize relative to a cold-atom prize.
responses.response: I take the 2016 argument seriously, and it is the objection I would find hardest to answer if I were not a condensed matter outsider. My reply is the one above: the 2016 prize rewarded topological phase transitions and Hall-type phases, and this candidate rewards symmetry-protected band topology realised in a real material by a specific experiment. I think that is a different claim, and the HgTe edge conductance is direct evidence of it. On B002, I agree it is a discovery about correlated matter and not just a platform, and the Mott transition and the microscope are decisive results. My difficulty is the same as yours: Cirac, Esslinger and Jaksch fall outside any three seats, and with five names credited a citation that names the field must also explain who is omitted. If the committee does not settle on B013, I would put B002 well ahead of B009, but I cannot yet argue for it over a candidate with a compact three-person credit.

responses.point: Pearce supports the trio and the 2D citation, objects that the wording should not say Kane and Mele predicted the HgTe effect, and as chair asks the committee for a single sentence distinguishing B013 from 2016.
responses.response: I agree with your wording point and I have kept it. The citation names the Z2 quantum spin Hall state and its first observation in HgTe quantum wells, without saying that Kane and Mele predicted the HgTe realisation, which is the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang step. For the chair's question on 2016, my sentence is that the 2016 prize recognised topological phase transitions and Hall-type phases, while this prize recognises time-reversal-protected band topology in real materials, first shown by protected edge conduction in HgTe. On your question about my conflict, I will take part in technical discussion of B009 if asked, because I know the physics, but I will not vote for or against any configuration that depends on it. My preferred configuration and both of my alternatives avoid it.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts that the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal can be left out of the credited names while the citation stays accurate, given that Zhang has died.
Whether a wording limited to the 2D quantum spin Hall state is considered a complete story, or whether the missing 3D work by Hasan will be read as a flaw in the final record.

Whether the one-sentence distinction from the 2016 topological-phases prize will satisfy outside readers, since I am a theorist from a different subfield and defer to the condensed matter members on how the HgTe edge-transport interpretation stands.
How much of the strong convergence on B013 comes from members reading each other's openings, as the chair noted, which I cannot separate from independent judgment.
statement.conflict_note: My disclosure is unchanged in substance. I am a theorist in superconducting circuits, I direct the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology at Chalmers, and I work closely with groups in this field, which makes B009 a candidate on which I am not neutral. I ranked it first in my opening, and I now withdraw it from my alternatives. In answer to the chair, I will not take part in any vote on a configuration that depends mainly on B009, and I will limit myself to technical answers if colleagues ask for them. I also have colleague links with Chalmers MC2 researchers, including Olsson, and Kroll is linked to WACQT, but none of this bears on B013, B025 or B006. I know of no collaboration with any credited person in B013.
